components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Small Header Button

components.name: Tool Grid

components.name: Highlighted Choice
components.description: The signature chosen state: a tilted highlighter swipe behind the option, never an outline.
components.css: .ds-choices{display:flex;gap:8px}.ds-choice{position:relative;height:36px;padding:0 12px;background:none;border:none;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1)}.ds-choice:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.05)}.ds-choice-on:hover{background:none}.ds-choice:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #000;outline-offset:2px}.ds-choice-label{position:relative;z-index:1;font:600 13px system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif;color:#000}.ds-highlight{position:absolute;inset:0;background:#FFE433;transform:rotate(-2deg);transform-origin:left center;border-radius:4px 10px 5px 12px;z-index:0}@keyframes ds-swipe{from{opacity:0;transform:rotate(-2deg) scaleX(0.5)}}.ds-choice-on .ds-highlight{animation:ds-swipe 160ms cubic-bezier(0.33,1,0.68,1)}

components.name: Color Ring
components.description: Color swatches: the one choice ringed instead of highlighted.
components.css: .ds-rings{display:flex}.ds-ring{width:44px;height:44px;display:grid;place-items:center;padding:0;background:none;border:none;cursor:pointer}.ds-ring span{width:28px;height:28px;border-radius:50%;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.2),0 0 0 4px #fff,0 0 0 6px transparent;transition:box-shadow 160ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1),transform 160ms}.ds-ring:hover span{box-shadow:0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.2),0 0 0 4px #fff,0 0 0 6px #C8CACF}.ds-ring-on span,.ds-ring-on:hover span{box-shadow:0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.2),0 0 0 4px #fff,0 0 0 6px #000}.ds-ring:active span{transform:scale(0.92)}.ds-ring:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #000;border-radius:50%}

components.name: Wordmark
components.description: Tuck in Anton, black on a full highlighter swipe, the same in both palettes.

narrative.overview:
Tuck treats every photo as a print laid on a pale light table, and the app as the stationery around it. The bars, the dock, and every sheet are white paper. Controls, labels, and the main action are black ink. The app's only color of its own is a highlighter-yellow swipe, drawn behind whatever is chosen: a tool, a font, a size, a format. Everything else stays neutral gray, so the photo's own colors read true.

The system is quick and decisive. People use Tuck one-handed, for jobs that take seconds, so the main action is always a solid black bar, the shape of a redaction. Targets are generous, every tool shows at once in two rows, and a press answers immediately. Expression lives in a few precise details: the swipe's slight tilt, the print's two shadows, and the Anton wordmark, which uses the same typeface as the meme captions people make with Tuck.

Night is the same system on a graphite table, not a darkroom. The paper turns charcoal and the ink turns off-white, but the highlighter stays the same yellow with black ink on it, so the mark and every chosen state look identical in both palettes. The palette is picked once at launch from the system setting and kept until the next launch.
keyCharacteristics: The photo is a print: it sits on a gray table with a contact shadow and a soft lift.
The UI is paper and ink: white bars, black labels, hairline edges.
The only color of the app's own is highlighter yellow, and it means "chosen".
Blue is reserved for anything drawn over the photo (selection, snap guides, detection picks), and red for destructive actions.
Controls use the platform's system font. Anton appears only in the wordmark and home's headings.

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: Yellow means "chosen", and nothing else is yellow. No yellow buttons, badges, or decoration. If two things on screen are yellow, each must be a chosen option.

rules.name: The Off-Limits Photo Rule
rules.body: The app's chrome never tints, frosts, or overlaps the photo with color. Only selection blue draws over it, and only to show what's selected or proposed.

rules.name: The Same Mark Rule
rules.body: The highlighter and its black ink are identical by day and at night. The wordmark, the icon, and every chosen state must look the same in both palettes.

rules.name: The Poster Only Rule
rules.body: Anton appears in the wordmark and home's headings, never on a button, label, or title. Literal font sizes are allowed only for Anton, font previews, and the text editor's hidden 16px input.

rules.name: The No Gray Label Rule
rules.body: A control's label is ink. Gray is for metadata, never for something you can press.

rules.name: The Print Rule
rules.body: Only prints and floating panels cast shadows. A bar, row, or button with a shadow is a bug.

dos: Do take every color from `colors` in `theme.ts`, which is the day or the night palette. Never write a literal that assumes one of them.
Do mark a chosen option with `<Highlight />` as the control's first child, and draw what's over it in `on-highlighter`.
Do keep one ink-bar primary action per screen, and make it the thing the user came to do.
Do draw anything over the photo in selection blue, with the dark halo under its lines.
Do take sizes from `typography`, corners from `radii`, and gaps from `space`.
Do give every tappable control at least a 44pt target, with `hitSlop` where the visible shape is smaller.
Do pad each bar and sheet's bottom content by the safe-area inset, and let its paper run to the screen's edge.
Do check every change in both palettes. The highlighter must look the same in each.
donts: Don't build a darkroom: no mostly black editor, and no gray controls that look disabled. Night is a graphite table, never pure black.
Don't mark a chosen option with an outline, an underline alone, or a filled chip. Chosen means highlighted. Only color swatches get a ring.
Don't add a second accent. No coral, no brand gradients, and no yellow outside a chosen state or the wordmark.
Don't put frosted or translucent glass over the photo. Panels are opaque paper.
Don't give bars, rows, or buttons a shadow. Only prints and floating panels lift.
Don't set controls in Anton or a caption font. The poster face belongs to the wordmark and home's headings.
